transcript.content: Extend this existing SVG board renderer with a user-selected fill color. Its current label output and tests must keep working.
Source offer offer-2ffeb707-1e3c-4e08-b85c-2f941fa52c68: How should the user-selected fill color be accepted while keeping the existing label output and tests working?

sourceOffers.scope: Extend SVG board renderer with user-selected fill color, preserving label output
sourceOffers.question: How should the user-selected fill color be accepted while keeping the existing label output and tests working?

options.label: Optional second fill argument, default preserves current label output
options.tradeoff: Smallest delta to existing render; callers without fill see no change, but fill handling stays minimal.
options.acceptanceExample: Given render('A') with no fill argument, output remains '<text>A</text>'; given render('A', 'red'), output adds fill without changing the label text.

options.label: Additive fill support guarded by existing label test
options.tradeoff: Keeps the current test as the compatibility gate, but requires new coverage only for the fill delta.
options.acceptanceExample: Given the existing test render('A') equals '<text>A</text>', it still passes; a new case render('A', 'blue') is checked separately for fill.

options.label: Preserve label output and add only fill-color handling
options.tradeoff: Directly addresses the documented limitation with no rewrite, but defers any broader renderer changes.
options.acceptanceExample: Given a user-selected fill color, the renderer emits the same label text plus fill; given no fill, output matches the prior label-only behavior.

source.quote: Current renderer supports labels but not a user-selected fill color. Preserve its existing label output.
